title: 63 deadlocks in five days
prompt: Client: Harbourline Commerce, a multi-tenant retail order platform with about 400 tenants. Database hlc-orders-prod: Azure SQL Database, Business Critical, Gen5, 16 vCores, compatibility level 160, READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. All times are UTC. Business hours are 07:30 to 18:00. The nightly batch must finish by 06:00. Evidence was collected from Mon 21 Sep to Sun 27 Sep 2026.
The application logs 9 to 16 deadlock errors (1205) on each business day. The client's DBA proposes NOLOCK hints, or
turning READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT off 'because it causes version conflicts'. Batch step 4 is one UPDATE of about 6.2M
rows of dbo.Inventory; since September it runs between about 07:00 and 09:00. Name the root cause of the deadlocks.

pattern.process_a: batch step 4 UPDATE: holds PAGE X locks, requests U on another page
pattern.process_b: dbo.usp_CreateOrder for an order with several lines: holds KEY X on one SKU row, requests U on a SKU row on a page that A holds

result.note: usp_CreateOrder updates the SKUs in the order in which the client sends the basket lines.

head_blocker.statement: Batch step 4: UPDATE i SET OnHand = i.OnHand - a.Qty FROM dbo.Inventory i JOIN stg.InventoryAdj a ON ... (about 6.2M rows)

blocked.statement: dbo.usp_CreateOrder: UPDATE dbo.Inventory SET Reserved = Reserved + @q WHERE Sku = @sku

required_facts.description: All 63 deadlocks happened while batch step 4 ran, and none outside it.
required_facts.example: All 63 deadlocks happened while batch step 4 was running (06:59 to 09:01); there were 0 outside it.

required_facts.description: The batch holds page locks while order creation updates SKU rows in basket order.
required_facts.example: The batch update holds PAGE X locks while usp_CreateOrder updates SKU rows in the order of the basket lines.

harmful_conclusions.description: Both sides are writers. NOLOCK changes nothing for them and risks wrong stock figures elsewhere.
harmful_conclusions.example: Add NOLOCK hints to the inventory queries.

harmful_conclusions.description: READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT is already ON and affects readers only. Turning it off adds reader-writer blocking and removes no deadlock.
With escalation disabled, a 6.2M-row update holds millions of locks and the page-level conflict stays.
The deadlocks need the batch to overlap business hours; they are not a platform or capacity fault.
